title: Conditional probability where you must build the given group
subtitle: Probability and conditional probability · 8 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **8 of the official questions in Probability and conditional probability are this one** — 0 Easy, 2 Medium, 6 Hard.
It is top-heavy: most versions are Hard, so it only earns study time once your target actually requires that tier.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- The condition doesn't match a single printed total.
- It says 'not in group k', 'at least N', or 'greater than or equal to', and so it covers several columns or rows.
- Or the data comes as proportions instead of counts, or as a word description to multiply out (like rows × items per row), or as a set of integers that you have to count yourself.
- These are usually Hard.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Rebuild the given group by adding every row or column in the condition, or by multiplying groups × items per group, or by counting the integers in the range.
- 2) Inside that group, count or add the part that also has the target trait.
- 3) Divide.
- If you only have proportions, use them as if they were counts, because the scaling cancels.

sections.heading: Where Desmos fits
body: It helps a little with arithmetic.
You can type the whole ratio, such as (a+b)/(a+b+c+d), in one line so you don't make adding mistakes along the way.
It doesn't help you set up the group.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You read 'at least N' as 'more than N' and drop the boundary bin.
You read 'not in group 2' as 'group 2'.
You use only one column of a combined condition.
Or you divide by the full total instead of the rebuilt group.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
You read 'at least N' as 'more than N' and drop the boundary bin.
You read 'not in group 2' as 'group 2'.
